page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head above the text, with the page number at its left. No marginal notes. Catchword "&" alone at the lower right, below the last line.

main_text.p: modo substituet, eo semper animo est, ut quicunque eue-tus substitutionis futurus sit, tamen substitutu malit, quàm agnatum suum sibi heredem esse. Itaque non formulæ ver-ba, sed testatoris uoluntas se-quenda est. D. An cùm pupillariter substituens verbo & formula pupillo substituit, re tamen malit hereditatem suam ad substitutum, quàm ad agnatum, quo poterit mo-do, peruenire. Quæ contro-uersia Veri & Marci constitutione sublata est: qua cauetur, ut etiam pupillari substi-tutione vulgaris cõtineatur: id est, ut qui dicit, si heres sit, &

page.notes: The page number reads "172" but the first digit and the last are slightly worn, so it is marked [?]. The running head is a heavy decorative line that I could not read letter by letter. In "euentus", the printed hyphen falls after "eue", so the break is marked as printed; the last letters are not fully clear. "pupillariter" has no printed hyphen at the line end and is written whole. The catchword "&" is the only word below the text.
